newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia upgrades, forestries drive Helsinki ahead.
newsitem.headline: Nokia upgrades, forestries drive Helsinki ahead.

text.p: Shares rose on Wednesday, the market buoyed by a clear return to record ground in Nokia and with dollar strength fuelling forestries ahead of the first results in the Finnish sector on Thursday, brokers said.
The FOX portfolio index rose 0.61 percent to recoup Tuesday's losses and end at 1,241.75, the HEX all-share index climbed 1.11 percent to 3,644.75.

Nokia made up over half volume, closing up 16.00 markka or over three percent at 487.90 just off an all-time high 488.00. Buyers returned amid a flurry of analyst upgrades after a bout of profit-taking in the wake of its H1 results, brokers said.

Metsa-Serla, which reports for H1 on Thursday, stood out on price, putting on 1.80 markka or nearly four percent to close at 48.20. Brokers said the stock was spurred by the dollar's rise and mounting expectations after Stora beat forecasts.
Analysts polled by Reuters expect a median 269 million markka profit for Metsa-Serla, a gain of about 20 percent on proforma H1 1996 at 223 million.
UPM was again active, adding 0.80 markka to 133.40 but brokers could still not identify any key factors. UPM's report is due next week, along with the bulk of Nordic forestries.
Also firm ahead of its H1 report on Thursday was TT Tieto.
The software and data group added 1.00 markka to 480.00 markka, generating heavier than usual trade at about one percent of the market total.
Analysts expect Tieto to show a H1 profit gain around 36 percent, to 116 million markka from 85.2 million in the year-ago period.
